risks.risk: Heavy sector concentration in wind energy
risks.note: The wind sector accounted for over 80% of revenues; management's own mitigation is that facilities are versatile enough to serve other large-casting applications with reasonable lead time, implying the concentration itself is structural.

Demand is concentrated among a handful of global wind OEMs (Vestas, Vayona/erstwhile Siemens Gamesa, GE, Nordex, Adani, Envision) and gearbox makers (Flender Drives, ZF Wind); the Company is actively adding customers (Senvion, GE India, Adani; onboarding Nordex and Envision) specifically to mitigate this concentration risk.

risks.risk: Commodity price volatility in key raw materials
risks.note: Input prices for pig iron and CRCA scrap are volatile and were further pressured by the West Asia conflict; the Company hedges via quarterly customer contracts, but there can be a one-quarter lag in passing on price changes, exposing near-term margins.
With exports at roughly 25-30% of revenue, currency movements are a structural risk; mitigated via Foreign Currency Term Loans and currency swap arrangements to create a natural hedge.
Availability of skilled labour, particularly for critical operations such as fettling, remains a challenge; the Company is pursuing automation to reduce dependence on manual processes.

risks.risk: Rising financial leverage from the capex programme
risks.note: The ₹217 crore capex programme was funded partly through debt; the Debt-Equity Ratio rose to 2.25 (from 1.45) and Interest Coverage Ratio fell to 2.37 (from 3.42), reflecting borrowings availed for the capital expenditure.

risks.risk: Execution/ramp-up risk on newly commissioned capacity
risks.note: FY26 profitability was already dented by higher outsourcing and operating costs, manpower/overhead costs, and discounted export pricing during the development phase of the in-house machining facility; expected margin benefits depend on successful utilisation ramp-up of the new foundry, machining and solar capacity through FY27.

themes.title: Renewable IPP / FDRE firm-power & storage
themes.need: DISCOMs mandating firm/round-the-clock RE make BESS + pumped-hydro the bid differentiator, and in Q1FY27 storage demand ran ahead of supply. ADANIGREEN has 3.5 GWh of BESS installed (+1.9 GWh at Khavda this quarter), targets 10+ GWh this fiscal and 50 GWh by FY30 on a thumb-rule INR 25-30 lakh of EBITDA per MWh against ~INR 1.5cr/MWh of capex, and has contracted essentially all merchant/C&I capacity to sibling AESL on 25-year (solar/wind) and 15-year (battery) fixed-price PPAs targeting ~15-16% IRR - a pivot from merchant builder to fixed-return contracted IPP, with evacuation (not panels) named as the binding constraint. JSWENERGY added 873 MW in Q1 and ~1.1 GW since April - 36% of its 3 GW FY27 target already banked, Tidong Hydro commissioned four months early - and raised INR 10,150cr, taking net leverage 5.2x to 4.95x. On the equipment side SERVOTECH said its BESS pack capacity is fully booked ('we are not able to meet the demand') and committed to 2x capacity in 6 months, 3x by 21-Mar-2027 and 10x within 2 years. ACMESOLAR/KPIGREEN/SUZLON/INOXWIND attach storage to solar/wind; NTPC/NHPC/SJVN/TATAPOWER drive pumped-hydro and utility-scale storage.
themes.driver: BESS capacity commissioning against demand two independent managements (ADANIGREEN, SERVOTECH) say already exceeds supply; FDRE/peak-power tender awards; merchant DAM prices (JSWENERGY: INR 4.40 -> INR 5.10/unit, +16%) on +8.5% Q1 power demand.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: SGIL is a foundry manufacturer of SG (spheroidal graphite) and CI (cast iron) castings, primarily supplying critical components to the global wind turbine, gearbox and general engineering industries.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: The Company manufactures SG & CI castings, operating as a single reportable segment, with the majority of output going into wind turbine components for global wind OEMs and gearbox manufacturers, and the remainder into general industrial castings for machinery, mining, plastic injection and pump applications. It serves both domestic and international customers, with long-term supply partnerships built over the years with several of the top global wind OEMs.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Global and Indian wind energy markets remain on a strong growth trajectory, with the West Asia conflict further accelerating renewable-energy installations
- India's emergence as a manufacturing hub for multinational OEMs is unlocking significant global demand for domestic casting manufacturers
- Depreciation of the Indian Rupee, particularly against the Chinese Yuan, is improving the competitiveness of Indian castings in global markets
- Geopolitical shifts, including regional tensions and trade wars, are increasing sourcing from India and strengthening export opportunities for Indian foundries
- New customer additions and product developments are broadening the Company's addressable market, backed by enhanced production capacity
- Ramp-up of the newly commissioned 20,000 TPA in-house machining facility and 10 MW captive solar plant is expected to drive margin expansion and cost optimisation from FY27 onward
- Company remains heavily dependent on the wind sector (over 80% of revenues), though facilities are versatile enough to serve other large-casting applications with reasonable lead time
- West Asia conflict is pressuring input raw-material prices; commodity costs are hedged via quarterly customer contracts, though there can be a one-quarter lag in passing on price changes
- FY26 revenue growth was muted due to project activities/operational disruption from the brownfield expansion, slower offtake from newly acquired Wind Domestic OEM customers, and lower OEM Export revenue during the product transition to higher-MW turbine platforms; Gearbox and Non-Wind segments partly offset this
- Executable order book for FY 2026-27 is projected to grow by over 33% compared to the previous year, surpassing the ₹500 crore mark

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: FY26 margin compression due to: (1) higher outsourcing during transition, (2) new facility overheads, (3) discounted export pricing (in-house machining not yet operational), (4) commodity/energy inflation from West Asia; FY27 margin recovery expected via utilization leverage, price pass-throughs, and INR depreciation benefit

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Debt-funded capex (₹160-165Cr net debt); focus on utilization optimization before new capex; dividend policy not disclosed; reinvestment prioritized over buybacks or dividends

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: FY 2025-26 was a transformational capex year for SGIL, marked by completion of a brownfield foundry expansion (foundry capacity raised from 30,000 TPA to 45,000 TPA, with a new production line and single-product weight capability raised from 23 MT to 30 MT), establishment of a new fettling and inspection facility sized for the enlarged 45,000 TPA capacity (with activities relocated from existing facilities), commissioning of new in-house machining and surface-treatment facilities with 20,000 TPA installed capacity (including new machining/coating processes and customer approvals for the facilities), and expansion of captive solar power capacity from 2 MW to 10 MW. The programme was executed over roughly 12-18 months and funded through the Rights Issue completed in October 2024, internal accruals and debt financing. In parallel, the Company developed 12 new products across major OEM customers for turbines up to 5 MW, to utilise the enhanced capacity. Management expects the benefits of ramping these newly commissioned facilities to progressively reflect in financial performance from FY 2026-27 onward.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Cautiously optimistic; acknowledges near-term headwinds but confident in FY27 margin recovery; emphasizes operational discipline, pricing power, and long-term capacity needs; management is proactive on customer diversification and cost control

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Long-term supply partnerships with six of the top 15 global wind OEMs (Vestas, Vayona/erstwhile Siemens Gamesa, GE, Nordex, Adani, Envision) plus Indian OEM Senvion
- Long-term contracts with major wind gearbox manufacturers Flender Drives and ZF Wind, diversifying beyond pure wind-turbine castings
- Tier-1 supplier relationships across industrial machinery, mining, plastic injection and pumps (Terex, Milacron, Wilo), giving facility versatility to redeploy capacity beyond wind with reasonable lead time
- Zero TRIR (safety incident rate) maintained for four consecutive years, supported by ISO 45001 certification
- 98% sand recycling through thermal and mechanical reclamation, reducing virgin raw material consumption and cost

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Commodity price volatility (steel, energy) with 1-2 quarter lag; geopolitical disruption in shipping routes (Middle East); ramp-up delays in new capacity; labor training and operational synchronization; legal dispute with MSCB over solar banking policy

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: 12 new product developments in FY26 (including for Vestas, L&T) significantly increase complexity but also revenue potential; machining utilization at 50% already despite only 30-40% product development complete — indicates faster-than-expected learning curve; INR depreciation vs Yuan (20%) is a bigger competitive advantage than vs USD (10%)

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Stay ahead of evolving wind industry requirements as the sector transitions to larger turbine platforms, through continuous investment in capacity, technology and capabilities
- Build long-term partnerships with leading global wind OEMs by delivering quality, reliability and engineering excellence
- Diversify beyond core wind-OEM castings into gearbox manufacturers (Flender Drives, ZF Wind) and industrial Tier-1 customers (mining, plastic injection, pumps) to reduce sector concentration
- Expand customer portfolio to mitigate concentration risk - added Senvion India, GE India and Adani, with Nordex …

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Guidance] "FY 27 is expected to have a ~33% revenue growth over FY 26", with the revenue-streams chart showing FY 26-27 P of 500 Rs Cr versus 376 Rs Cr in FY 25-26, "Based on executable Order Book Projection" — management flags this projection "may be subject to change based on market conditions".
- [Guidance] "Despite moderation in Q1, FY27 PBDIT margin is expected to improve by >300 bps, driven by higher volumes, increased export contribution and growing contributions from in-house machining."
- [Industry - wind] "India's installed wind capacity to more than double from 51 GW in 2026 to 107 GW by 2030" and "Global cumulative capacity projected to exceed 2 TW by 2030, driven by record-breaking annual installations" (source: GEWC Global Wind Report 2026).
- [Industry - castings] 2024 casting market of 110 Mn MT total, "Global: $ 160 bn" and "India: $ 13.2 bn"; large casting demand split "Wind : 1.5 Mn MT" and "Non-Wind: ~6 Mn MT" (sources: Indian Institute of Foundrymen, Foundry Planet).
- [Exceptional item] The income statement records exceptional items described as "statutory provision for new labour code" — 0.01 Rs Crore for the quarter ended 31.03.26 and 0.65 Rs Crore for the year ended 31.03.26.
